clue.text: A woman's song about British plant collections

indicators.note: the phrase 'A woman's song' wraps around the abbreviation for British

parts.note: her is the possessive of a woman
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A woman sings an aria about the plant collections of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbaria, the plural of herbarium, are collections of dried and preserved plant specimens.

clue.text: Acquit former partner on single charge

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
one means single
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A court clears someone's ex who faced a single charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to declare them free of blame, which is what acquitting does.

clue.text: A second dog climbing tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: lab is short for Labrador, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A second dog is seen scrambling up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns A + S + LAB upwards, giving the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree famous for its very light wood.

clue.text: Professional soldier's uniform

definitions.meaning: a member of the permanent standing army, as opposed to a reservist

explanation.surface: A career soldier's kit is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-time soldier is called a regular, and something uniform is steady and even in pattern.

clue.text: Revise commercial involving soldiers

indicators.note: the advert takes in, or involves, the soldiers

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rework an advert featuring troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to make changes to it, which is to revise it.

clue.text: But this parasite may make us cross!

definitions.text: But this parasite may make us cross!

parts.words: But this parasite may make us cross!
parts.note: a check mark is the opposite of a cross on a marked answer, so the bloodsucker is set against the cross; the parasite also annoys us

explanation.surface: A biting parasite irritates us.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the marks on an exam paper: right answers get one mark, wrong ones a cross, so the parasite's name is the opposite of what makes us 'cross'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a bloodsucking parasitic arachnid, and also the mark used against a cross.

clue.text: Fruit primarily taken by artist — not Michel

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word taken
not signals that the name Michel is dropped from the artist's name

parts.note: Michelangelo, the Renaissance painter and sculptor
taken as written, the first part of the artist's name

explanation.surface: A fruit is chosen by a painter, though not by someone called Michel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link; the artist is the Renaissance master whose full name opens with Michel, so 'not Michel' leaves the rest of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit, a hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Senior officer's pass

definitions.meaning: The abbreviation for colonel, a senior army officer
a mountain pass, the high gap between peaks

explanation.surface: A senior officer's travel permit is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Col abbreviates colonel, and as a word it is a low point on a ridge between two peaks.

clue.text: Charlie's fruit dessert?

definitions.meaning: a charlie is British slang for a silly person, an idiot
a cold pudding of puréed fruit mixed with cream or custard

explanation.surface: Charlie's favourite pudding is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is an idiot, which 'a right Charlie' means in British slang, and also a creamy fruit pudding.

clue.text: Garden pest misused energy, consuming tops of flowers

indicators.note: the rearranged letters eat up, or take in, the other piece
energy put to wrong use is reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the top letters of the word flowers are F and L

explanation.surface: A garden bug wastes its energy eating the heads off the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges the letters of energy into GREENY; 'tops' is plural, so two opening letters of 'flowers' go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are aphids, small sap-sucking insects that infest garden plants.

clue.text: Retired woman and man selected for special duty

indicators.note: retired here means drawn back, so the names are read in reverse

parts.note: Delia is a woman's name
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A retired woman and a man are picked for a special assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reverses DELIATED, the two names together.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail a soldier is to assign them to a particular task, so detailed means assigned.

clue.text: Antelope's endless combination of style and vigour

indicators.note: endless means the antelope's name loses its final letter

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope is admired for its stylish vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan means flair and energetic panache, a mix of stylishness and vigour.

clue.text: Impressive undertaking for Bobby?

definitions.meaning: a bobby is a British police officer, whose job includes taking criminals into custody

explanation.surface: A policeman's task is described as impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is everyday British slang for a police constable, named after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arresting grabs the attention, and arresting suspects is a police officer's work.

clue.text: Is its rough justice dispensed by leaps and bounds?

definitions.text: Is its rough justice dispensed by leaps and bounds?

parts.words: Is its rough justice dispensed by leaps and bounds?
parts.note: an unofficial, unfair tribunal is pictured literally as a court run by hopping marsupials

explanation.surface: Asks whether swift, rough justice is handed out in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by leaps and bounds' usually means rapidly; here it pictures hopping animals presiding over the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court is a sham tribunal that ignores proper legal procedure; kangaroos move by leaping.

clue.text: VIP taking old woman on river

parts.note: gran, short for grandmother, an old woman
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A dignitary takes an elderly lady out on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank or importance, originally a Spanish nobleman.

clue.text: Subdue section of media after work

indicators.note: the media section comes after the work, so beneath it in this down entry

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
the press is the part of the media made up of newspapers

explanation.surface: Part of the media is told to calm down after doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to keep people down by harsh rule, to subjugate them.

clue.text: Act as volunteers, getting second highest grade

parts.note: to be something is to act in that role, as in 'be the host'
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers earn a B grade for their efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta, the Greek second letter, is used for a second-class grade in marking.

clue.text: Stupidity of obnoxious person reversing round trees

indicators.note: the turned-round word goes around the trees
reversing means the word for the obnoxious person is read backwards

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person
pines are trees

explanation.surface: A nasty person backs his car round some trees, stupidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' makes DOS, which 'round' wraps around the trees; the surface pictures a driver reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopiness is the state of being dopey, slow-witted or dull.

clue.text: Small person's notes about conflict

indicators.note: the two notes surround the word for conflict

parts.note: D and F are musical notes
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A short person writes notes about a conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwarf is an unusually small person, or a small being of folklore.

clue.text: Man penning volume, a work of fiction

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the man's name holds the other letter

parts.note: Noel is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man writes a book, a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a long fictional prose narrative.

clue.text: Male bird identifying poisonous plant

parts.note: a man is a male person
a drake is a male duck

explanation.surface: A male duck is spotted near a toxic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a Mediterranean plant of the nightshade family with a forked root, highly toxic.

clue.text: Single tool? The lot, by the sound of it

indicators.note: signals a word that is said like the one meaning the lot

parts.note: all means everything, the lot

explanation.surface: Asks whether one tool might sound like the whole set.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the playful contrast: a single tool sounds like 'the lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood; 'single' means just one of them.

clue.text: Conceited individual originally carried in commercial vehicle

indicators.note: the letter is carried inside the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a commercial vehicle

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of individual

explanation.surface: A conceited person was first driven around in a delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain means excessively proud of oneself, especially of one's looks.

clue.text: Bawdy university sportsman

definitions.meaning: at Oxford and Cambridge, a person who has represented the university at sport earns a ...

explanation.surface: A rude university athlete is described.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, a Blue is awarded to someone who competes for the university in a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means indecent or smutty, and an Oxbridge sporting representative is called a Blue.

clue.text: Join convict, English, in body of plane

parts.note: to fuse is to join together
a lag, or old lag, is British slang for a convict

explanation.surface: An English convict is asked to join others inside an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft, holding crew and passengers.
